newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: EU condemns IRA police killings.
newsitem.headline: EU condemns IRA police killings.

text.p: European Union leaders have condemned the IRA's killing of two Northern Irish policemen on Monday and extended their sympathy to the victims' families.

"The European Union heads of state and government meeting in Amsterdam have heard with horror of the murder of two policemen by the provisional IRA in Northern Ireland...," the leaders said in a statement issued by a spokesman on Tuesday at their summit in Amsterdam.
The statement went on: "They condemn this callous act of terrorism and extend their deepest sympathy to the families of the victims.
"They reaffirmed their abhorrence of terrorist violence in all its forms, whereever it may occur and their solidarity with the governments and people who suffer its effects."

The killings, which a caller using a known IRA code word told a Belfast radio station had been carried out by the group's "North Armagh Brigade", dealt a heavy blow to already faltering hopes of a peace settlement for the British-ruled province.
The United States joined Britain and Ireland in condemning the attack, which White House spokesman Mike McCurry called "an outrageous act of cowardice, an outrageous act of terrorism".

Blair repeated his condemnation of the IRA on Tuesday, saying the ambush was designed to derail peace efforts. "The reason why President Clinton is so angry, the reason why we are so angry, the reason why the European Union here took the unusual step of issuing a unanimous statement condemning utterly these atrocities yesterday is because everybody knows...that we were trying to bring about a situation in which there could be a lasting political settlement," he told reporters in Amsterdam.
"We were making every effort to be constructive and this was a deliberate act to frustrate that process going forward."
Blair on Monday ruled out any fresh meeting between government officials and the IRA's political wing, Sinn Fein.
